text.boundary_case: Consider 11 points on the surface of a sphere with radius r. The distance between two points on the surface is equal to the angle subtended by those points at the center of the sphere, multiplied by r. If all points are equally spaced around the sphere, then the maximum distance between any two points will occur when they are diametrically opposite, i.e., 2r. Therefore, the minimum sum of inverse pair distances over 11 distinct points on the unit sphere in three dimensions can be found by placing them at regular intervals around a great circle (a circle on the sphere that is centered at one of its poles). In this case, the distance between any two points will be less than or equal to 2r. Since r = 1, the maximum possible value for the sum of inverse pair distances over 11 distinct points on the unit sphere in three dimensions is 22.
text.gap: The subclaim states that the minimum sum of inverse pair distances over 11 distinct points on the unit sphere in three dimensions is bounded below by 5062494437/125000000. However, this bound assumes that the 11 points are placed at regular intervals around a great circle, which may not be the case. Therefore, this subclaim does not imply the target.
